item.title: The Ripple Effect of Going for It
item.description: Can you learn to captain a yacht at 62 and turn it into a world-traveling lifestyle? Absolutely! Below, Sine Maria shares a first-hand account of her family’s latest charter with Dream Yacht in the Balearic Islands. Read on for an inspiring look at courage, partnership, and what happens when you say yes to a new adventure on the water. The Ripple Effect of Going for It On breaking into worlds you weren’t born into, and what happens when you actually do the thing. By: Good Life Designed and Sine Maria If there’s one thing I’ve learned from my mom, it’s that life has so much to offer and the limit of your world is only limited by your ability to keep expanding. In the middle of the pandemic, as part of our collective pause, she and I decided to go through the whole Good Life Designed program together again. It was through that process that she decided she wanted to be closer to nature, swim more, and learn how to sail. She didn’t grow up around sailing, knew it was costly and a bit of a boys club, but always admired the access it gave those who knew how. That hobby could take you anywhere in the world. The world of sailing requires a unique blend of resources, courage, technical education, practice, and willing crew members to go along for the ride and be there while you figure things out on your first trips alone. It thrives behind heavy yacht club doors that some are born with access into – but most don’t even know exist. The dream of being certified as a sailor has an even smaller niche- attracting those who thrive on the pressure to read and respond to the chaos of the elements at sea while holding the responsibility of passengers’ lives in their hands. Now that I have experienced the reward that comes with that kind of responsibility – I see the draw. Breaking Into a World You Weren’t Born Into I tried to look into data about women certified sailors but couldn’t find any credible data because no one seems to be particularly interested in that stat – however I can tell you there aren’t many. Sailing, just due to the nature of it, the time it requires, the unease that comes with the experience, especially as you’re getting your first solo trips under your belt, is enough to send anyone right over the edge. It’s heady, it’s overwhelming, it’s complicated, it’s technical, and it feels uncertain and dangerous before you’re skilled and experienced enough to feel truly comfortable and at ease on the water. When Pernille got the ping to learn to sail, the biggest question was how, as a 62-year-old woman, was she going to do it. She tried visiting yacht clubs but as someone who wasn’t interested in the social component and was really looking for the technical skills to captain her own ship, it didn’t feel like the best place to spend her time or money. The classes and day sail opportunities to get out on the water were nice, but if she really wanted to learn everything she needed to, she needed something different. She came across Nautilus Sailing, a week-long course in the Sea of Cortez that would teach you everything you need to know about sailing and cap off the week with a test that would certify you to sail on your own anywhere in the world. My dad at the time was in the most stressful period of his career, navigating his independent school and their 400 families through Covid. Using his coveted spring break to learn to navigate another set of uncharted territories felt not quite like the vacation he needed. But he took a leap of his own and joined her anyway. They spent a week disconnected from everything to focus on learning the thing that would later give them access to the life they live now – barely imaginable to them then. Heading out on what feel like once-in-a-lifetime week long sailing experiences all over the world with friends and family. item.title: Discover the Remote National Parks of the Bahamas: The Exumas
item.description: Welcome back to our Bahamas Series! In this episode, we’re setting course for the National Parks of The Bahamas where untouched natural beauty abounds and every stop promises to leave a lasting impression. The Bahamas are more than just white-sand beaches and turquoise waters; they’re also home to an extraordinary network of marine and island national parks, many of which are only accessible by boat. For yacht charter guests looking to explore beyond the typical island hop, the national parks in the Exumas offer pristine nature, vibrant coral reefs, wildlife sanctuaries, and secluded anchorages you won’t find in any resort brochure. With a Dream Yacht charter, you can step into these untouched worlds aboard your own private yacht, creating a one-of-a-kind sailing itinerary through some of the Bahamas’ most spectacular marine preserves. Why Charter a Yacht to Explore These Parks? Most of these national parks are remote, undeveloped, and unreachable by land. That means fewer crowds, healthier reefs, and a level of tranquility that’s become rare in the modern Caribbean. Chartering a yacht, bareboat or crewed, is your ticket to experience them on your own schedule, with the luxury of anchoring in protected coves and swimming in some of the clearest waters on Earth. The Exumas: Untouched Beauty Off the Beaten Path Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park Spanning over 176 square miles, this is the crown jewel of Bahamian marine conservation—and it’s boat-access only. No fishing, no anchoring on the reefs, and no development: just nature in its rawest form. You’ll find rare sea life, blue holes, sandbars, and hiking trails on uninhabited cays. Moorings are available for overnight stays. Highlights Snorkel the underwater cave at Thunderball Grotto (yes, the one from the James Bond film). Hike Boo Boo Hill for sweeping views and legendary sailor lore. Kayak through mangroves or relax on Shroud Cay’s winding tidal creeks. Moriah Harbour Cay National Park Just south of Georgetown, this park protects 22,833 acres of pristine beaches, mangroves, and a rich variety of birds and marine life. It’s an ideal anchorage for yacht charters exploring southern Exuma. The shallow flats are also great for bonefishing and kiteboarding. Discover The Exumas Create Your Own Park-Hopping Sailing Itinerary With Dream Yacht, you can craft a custom itinerary that connects these remote national parks. Whether you’re chartering from Marsh Harbour in the Abacos or from our Exuma base in Nassau. Combine snorkeling, hiking, beachcombing, and stargazing all in one seamless, sea-bound adventure. Make sure to always check local regulations and pay the required park fees so that this beauty can be protected for generations to come. Explore The Bahamas Sustainable Sailing, Natural Wonders As stewards of the sea, Dream Yacht is proud to support sustainable yacht tourism. When visiting these parks, we encourage all guests to respect local guidelines: use mooring balls where available, avoid single-use plastics, and leave only footprints (or wake trails) behind. These parks exist thanks to decades of protection and the work of the Bahamas National Trust . Your visit helps fund their continued preservation and ensures these wild places remain for generations to come. Take a moment to briefly step into the Bahamas for a look at what awaits you with this video. Plan Your National Park Yacht Adventure Today Explore the Bahamas like few ever do. Whether you want a relaxed week of snorkeling and sunsets or an ambitious island-hopping itinerary through protected waters, Dream Yacht can help you make it happen. Get in touch today to start planning your yacht charter through the stunning national parks of the Abacos and Exumas—and discover a Bahamas you’ve never seen before. item.title: 7 Incredible, Lesser-Known Places In Greece To Visit
item.description: An azure paradise awaits you on a Greece sailing vacation . From sun-kissed shores and cerulean waters to alluring historical landmarks, the country’s 6,000 islands create the perfect backdrop for a once-in-a-lifetime holiday. The list of Greece places to see is nearly infinite, but with a yacht charter, exploring some of its hidden gems is easy. Ready to plan the ultimate off-the-beaten-track itinerary? With our Greece yacht charter bases in Athens , Lavrion , Kos , Lefkas , and Corfu , the only limit is your imagination! We’ve unearthed 7 secret spots where tourists are few and the possibilities are endless. Keep reading to get inspired for your one-of-a-kind Greece sailing vacation. 7 Lesser-Known Places In Greece To Visit Spetses: small and exclusive While nearby Hydra has long stolen the spotlight in the Sporadic islands, the lesser known Greek island of Spetses is a destination worth a second look. Full of neoclassical mansions, scenic landscapes, cobblestone streets and secluded swimming spots to while away the day — Spetses could just steal your heart. “The island of perfumes”, as it was named by the Venetians or “Pityousa” (which in ancient Greek means “full of pine-trees”), is a beautiful, car-free island (only taxis and delivery vehicles are allowed) with numerous wonderful sandy beaches and lovely secluded bays. Discover Agia Paraskevi, with its picturesque church – considered by many to be the most beautiful beach on the island. The island is home to several historical landmarks, including the Poseidonion Grand Hotel and the Bouboulina Museum, which offer insight into Spetses’ rich history. Stroll the old port, on the waterfront, and experience the freshest fish and seafood at this traditional taverna. Lake Vouliagmeni: Athens’ most underrated day trip Another unique destination to add to the beginning or end of your Greece sailing vacation is Lake Vouliagmeni. This haven of natural health, spa, and mineral baths has been healing visitors for thousands of years! You can visit it on a day trip from Athens , stop by from nearby islands, or take advantage of local 5-star accommodations. Fed by underground currents filtered through Mount Hymettus, the lagoon is known for its ancient hydrotherapy and physiotherapy properties. Eczema, neuralgia, headaches, arthritis, lumbago, sciatica, and many other ailments are all said to be healed by the waters. You can swim in the lake, lounge on the shores, or stop by a spa to take full advantage of the lake’s magic. Although it’s easy to overlook mainland adventures and dive head-first into Greece’s best sightseeing places on the island, you won’t regret visiting Lake Vouliagmeni. Tinos: the Hidden heart of the Cyclades The Cyclades is the cluster of Greek southeast of the mainland. You’ve already heard of Santorini, Naxos, and Mykonos, but the Cyclades are also home to Tinos, a pristine, untouched paradise. Writers, poets, philosophers, and religious pilgrims have long been attracted to Tinos for its tranquil landscapes and peaceful charm. Christian Orthodox Greeks consider the island sacred, but any visitor will be enchanted by its quiet beauty. If you’re on the hunt for empty beaches, Isternia, Apigania, and Koumelas will be your favorites. Rohari is a livelier option with more restaurants and bars. A bit more inland, you’ll find architecturally inspiring villages like Pyrgos, known as the ‘marble heart’ of Tinos. For a lesson in art history, stop by Pyrgos’ Museum of Marble Crafts or the historic home of world-famous sculptor Yannoulis Chalepas. For a taste of authentic Greek culture and history, it doesn’t get better than Tinos! The Diapontia Islands: Off Corfu’s beaten path Corfu is a hub for tourists and a Greece yacht charter location with Dream Yacht Worldwide, but hidden gems are abundant in the region.
